# bsllmner-viewer

> Ontology-mapped annotations of public BioSamples, linked to their SRA Experiments and BioProjects. bsllmner-mk2 extracted cell lines, cell types, tissues, diseases, drugs, genetic perturbations, and ChIP antigens from the free-text BioSample attributes with a large language model (LLM). bsllmner-mk2 then mapped each value to an ontology term. This site queries, counts, and exports those annotations. The annotations can be wrong. Each annotation has a status that tells how its term was chosen, or why it has none.

Use the JSON API rather than the web pages. Every result that the UI shows is also an API result.

## Links

- [Swagger UI](/api): the operations, with requests that you can try
- [OpenAPI document](/api/openapi.json): every operation, parameter, and response property, and the cause and the remedy of each error
- [Full rules](/llms-full.txt): the API specification and the data model in one file, for the rules that the recipes below name

## Conditions

Every query takes one condition string, `q`: `field:value`, `field:"phrase"`, `field:[a TO b]`, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, and parentheses. Text without a field is a keyword. The value of a term field is a term ID, not a label. A condition without `organism_id` matches BioSamples of every organism. `GET /api/dataset` lists the fields, the target assays, and the status groups.

- `disease:"MONDO:0007254"` matches breast cancer and every descendant term.
- `cell_line:"CVCL:0030" AND library_strategy:ATAC-seq` matches the ATAC-seq SRA Experiments of HeLa BioSamples.
- `organism_id:9606 AND date_published:[2015-01-01 TO 2020-12-31]` matches human BioSamples published from 2015 to 2020.
- `disease_status:unmapped` matches BioSamples whose disease value has no ontology term.
- `"breast cancer" AND NOT organism_id:10090` matches BioSamples that mention breast cancer and are not mouse.

## Recipes

A recipe that relies on a rule names the heading of /llms-full.txt that has the rule.

- Find a term ID: `GET /api/terms?field=disease&query=breast%20cancer`. Use the `termId` of a hit in a condition. `q` is the condition, and `query` is the search text of this operation. A gene is an NCBI Gene ID, so the human and the mouse gene of one symbol are different terms.
- Count: the BioSamples of a condition are `pagination.total` of `GET /api/entries/biosample?q=<q>&perPage=1`. For SRA Experiments or BioProjects, take `total` of `GET /api/distribution?field=library_strategy&q=<q>&unit=sra-experiment` (or `unit=bioproject`). See "Counting".
- Count per status group: count `(<q>) AND <field>_status:<group>` as in "Count", for `mapped`, `unmapped`, and `no_value`. A condition names a group. An entry shows the status of each annotation. See "Annotation status".
- Count per year: `GET /api/trend?q=<q>&yearFrom=2015&yearTo=2020` gives `total` for each year of publication. Add `field=disease` to get a line for each of the top diseases in `series`. See "Trend".
- Find gaps: `GET /api/crosstab?row=tissue&col=library_strategy&q=<q>` gives the observed and the expected count of each pair. `classification` marks the pairs far below or above the expectation. See "Expected counts in cross-tabulations".
- Get accessions: `GET /api/export/accessions/{type}?q=<q>` lists the accessions of one type, one per line after a header line that starts with `#`. `{type}` is a value of `AccessionType` in the OpenAPI document, such as `sra-run`. See "Entries".
- Get the BioSamples with their annotations: `GET /api/export/entries/biosample?q=<q>&format=tsv`, or `format=ndjson` for one JSON item per line. An export sends every match, so the export of a broad condition can take minutes. If an export stops before its end, then it is incomplete, whatever its status. See "Entries" and "Errors".
- Find the BioSample of an SRA Run, or of any other accession: `GET /api/entries/biosample?q=SRR11745799`. An accession is a keyword. See "Keywords".
- Get the same numbers as the UI: the `q` of a URL of `/entries` is the `q` of the API. The `tab` of the URL names the operation: `samples` is `GET /api/entries/biosample`, `projects` is `GET /api/projects`, `distribution` is `GET /api/distribution` for each field, `heatmap` is `GET /api/crosstab`, and `trend` is `GET /api/trend`. A URL without `tab` shows `samples`. The UI adds `facetSelfExclude=true` to the projects, the distribution, the cross-tabulation, the trend, and the term search. With `facetSelfExclude=true`, an operation counts the values of a field without the conditions on that field. The entry list and the counts of the whole condition use `q` itself. See "Self-exclusion".
- Read the other parameters of a URL of the UI: the UI does not write a parameter to the URL if the parameter has its default value. For these defaults, the API has another default or none, so send them: `perPage=20` for `samples` and `projects`, `row=cell_line` and `col=library_strategy` for `heatmap`, and `trend_field=disease` for `trend`. Some parameters of the URL have other names in the API: `row_terms` is `rowElements`, `col_terms` is `colElements`, `trend_field` is `field`, `trend_terms` is `elements`, `trend_from` is `yearFrom`, and `trend_to` is `yearTo`. Other parameters, such as `unit`, `row`, `col`, `sort`, `page`, and `perPage`, have the same names in the API. A parameter that changes only the display, such as `color`, has no API parameter. See "URLs".
- Check whether a term has descendants: `descendantCount` of its hit in `GET /api/terms` is above 0. A term without descendants matches only itself. A root term has an empty `parents`, even if it has descendants. See "Term hierarchy".
- Keep and cite the dataset version: counts change with every build. Record `datasetVersion` (`name`, `createdAt`, `model`, `digest`) from a JSON response, with the address of the API and the date. An export names the same version, without `model`, in its `X-Dataset-Version` header. See "Conventions".

Errors are problem documents. The `type` of a 400 or a 503 ends with a slug, and the OpenAPI document gives the cause and the remedy of each slug. Send only a few requests at the same time. If a response with status 429 or 503 has a `Retry-After` header, then wait for the number of seconds in the header, and send the request again.
